previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent abdominal pain and nausea/vomiting that returned after eating tacos, following a recent hospital discharge. She reported collapsing at home in her vomit, prompting re-evaluation. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology, consistent with prior unremarkable studies. Pain and nausea were managed with IV fluids, Dilaudid, and Zofran, with gradual advancement to oral intake. Her chronic pancreatitis was considered the likely contributor, though no active inflammation was seen. A mild Sjogren’s flare with facial erythema and low-grade fever was noted but remained asymptomatic. She tolerated a soft diet, had no pain, and was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications and follow up with her PCP and rheumatologist. H. pylori treatment was deferred pending outpatient coordination.

radiology_notes.text:
CT OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  Right upper quadrant and epigastric tenderness to palpation. 
History of prior pancreatic resection, and splenectomy.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, most recently CT of the abdomen and pelvis from
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast
only, including multiplanar reformations.

CT ABDOMEN:  Visualized lung bases are clear.  Post-surgical change from prior
distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy is stable.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding, or other evidence of pancreatitis.  Remaining pancreatic
parenchymal is normal in appearance.  Intra-abdominal parenchymal organs and
vasculature are otherwise normal in appearance.  There is no free air, free
fluid, or abnormal intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS:  Pelvic loops of large and small bowel and genitourinary structures
are normal.  There is no free pelvic fluid or abnormally enlarged pelvic or
inguinal lymph node.

Visualized skeletal structures are unchanged.  Congenital nonunion of the
posterior elements at L5 is unchanged.  

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of pancreatitis.  Stable post-surgical appearance
status post distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy.  No acute intra-abdominal
process.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with history of pancreatitis, status post partial
pancreatectomy and total splenectomy, now presenting  with right upper
quadrant pain and negative ___ sign.  Evaluate for biliary disease.

COMPARISON:  ___.

RUQ ULTRASOUND:  The liver is normal in echotexture without focal lesion. The
gallbladder is nondistended, without evidence of gallstones.  There is no
pericholecystic fluid.  The CBD is normal in caliber measuring about 3 mm in
diameter.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation.  The pancreas is seen truncated, consistent with pancreatectomy.
There is no ascites.  There is normal hepatopetal portal venous flow.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of obstructive biliary disease.  Patent portal vein.
No evidence of acute cholecystitis.
